_comment: capreq slug -> the capability requirement's identifier in Jama Connect.
Replaces capability-jira.json, deleted 2026-09-05. Jira Initiatives,
Objectives and Epics are being retired: ASI DevOps now syncs Jama
'User Story' to Jira 'Story' for sprint tracking, and the relationship from
a story up to the PRAK System Requirement it supports lives in Jama. The
capability layer has no Jira issue to point at any more, so the tiles and
the landing-page capability table point at Jama instead.
ALL 15 capabilities are listed, not the 9 that had a Jira Initiative. Jama
is the requirements system of record, so every capreq exists there; the
9/15 split was a Jira artefact and does not carry over.
This is a hand-maintained INPUT, like tracker-schema.json - not a build
product. It is the one thing about a capability prak-v-model does not yet
carry; cap_id, title and priority are all read from capreq frontmatter. If a
`jama-id` field is added to that frontmatter the reader already prefers it
and this file can be deleted, exactly as capability-jira.json was.
A value may be a bare Jama item id, substituted into url_template, or a
complete URL, used verbatim. Bare ids are preferred - one place to change if
the Jama host or perspective ever moves. An empty value renders the tile
with no link and is named on stderr.
In Jama a capability requirement is keyed by its prd-id (CAP-nn) and a system
requirement by its sysreq slug in the External ID field - see the
jama-import-workbooks skill in prak-v-model.
